summary: Observation of the movement of unknown aircraft.
description: witness reports that in July sometime between 1970 and 1973 (his recollection of the exact date of the sighting is imprecise, so we date it to July 1, 1970), around 9 PM, he saw a saucer-shaped aircraft, white or aluminum in color, approaching at an altitude of 300 or 400 meters. It measured between 6 and 8 meters in diameter and moved very slowly in a broken line from right to left. A beam of light emanated from two powerful spotlights located at the front. Calling members of his family, they saw the aircraft disappear at very high speed, silently, and in a 45° upward trajectory. A second aircraft then appeared: shaped like a white or aluminum cigar, about thirty meters in diameter, and arriving silently at the same altitude as the first. About thirty portholes allowed a soft, dim light to be seen inside. It moved very slowly in a straight line and disappeared, hidden by the treetops. The two aircraft were coming from the north-northwest and heading south-southeast. The witness mentions a newspaper article about lights appearing that evening at Bordeaux airport. This very old testimony provides surprising details; however, we lack information, and it is too old to conduct an investigation.

summary: A ball of white light that appeared to follow and pass an airplane.
description: Around 10 p.m., from the terrace of their home, two people observed the arrival of the Caravelle jet from Guadeloupe in the sky. Their attention was drawn to a white luminous phenomenon that initially appeared to follow the aircraft. At very high speed, this ball of light overtook the plane in a straight line and disappeared to the west. No unusual noise was heard during the brief observation (3 to 5 seconds). This event was reported several years later, and the witness specified that the observation likely occurred between the second half of 1969 and before July 1970 (we therefore date it to January 1, 1970). No other similar accounts of this phenomenon have been recorded in Martinique during this period, and we lack further information about it.
